title: Assembly of the fixed Cartier boundary equation and its Chern endpoint comparison
statement: Let all source and endpoint data be as in supportedFiniteBoundaryCartierEquation [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-supported-finite-boundary-cartier-equation] and let a be a normalized finite frame. If that fixed Cartier boundary equation holds and a.cartierMap for the canonical residue Cartier class equals finiteChernComposite at diagonalPic(Y) [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-finite-chern-composite], then finiteBoundaryEquation holds [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-finite-boundary-equation]. No finite-cycle or Chern normalization hypothesis is assumed by this purely logical assembly lemma.

source.place: paragraph (2), finite Cartier normalization and forget supports, before the divisor line is decomposed; diagonal-limit clause (3), and classes proof (3)

proof.text: Unfold the two named boundary equations. Their source, presentation and root comparison factors are identical. The generic endpoint-transport lemma carries the supported boundary equation along the supplied equality of its Cartier and Chern endpoints. This proves the desired equation without any new mathematical hypothesis.
